report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward culinary/restaurant content and a more formal “professional/technical” register relative to Model A.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells (layers ~17–25, positions 1–4) are dominated by cooking/restaurant vocabulary: “Cooking,” “cooking,” “Restaurant,” “restaurant,” “kitchen,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “baking,” “Bake/Baked,” “Cake,” “microwave,” “culinary,” “Professional/Professional Chef.” This cluster appears consistently across many layers/positions.
- Alongside that, there is a strong pull toward formal/professional/technical/academic terms: “Professional,” “professional,” “Technical/technical,” “Engineering,” “Innovation,” “dissertation,” “sciences,” “doctoral,” “molecular,” “laboratory,” “quantitative,” “preventive,” “practitioner,” which suggests a more formal/industry/academic register.
- The difference norm concentrates in mid-to-late layers (peaking around layers 21–25, especially at pos1), consistent with higher-level semantic/style features rather than surface tokenization artifacts.
- Patchscope readouts are unavailable here, so the conclusion rests on the consistent thematic pull in the logit-lens readouts and where the norm is concentrated.

I cannot name a specific training objective, but the semantic tilt is clear: compared to A, B preferentially points toward culinary/restaurant topics and a professional/technical style.
